title: State shareholdings management — 7 of 21 ownership-strategy measures unmet across three ministries
money_note: 235.6bn CZK paid from the state budget to state-held companies 2020-2024 (audit's own headline figure), converted at 24.5 CZK/EUR, the rate the corpus already uses for NKU records
summary: NKU audit 25/03, published in Vestnik 3/2026 on 13 August 2026, found the finance, industry and agriculture ministries did not exercise the state's ownership rights in line with the 2020 State Ownership Policy Strategy: seven of its 21 measures were never delivered, and the finance ministry classified two companies as strategic that the state did not need. The audited portfolio was 37 companies worth 127bn CZK at 31 December 2024, which drew 235.6bn CZK of budget money and returned 145.2bn CZK of dividends over 2020-2024.
notes: Conclusion PDF parsed, not the RSS headline (SCANS.md demand-scan item 1). Responsible bodies named by the audit: Ministerstvo financi, Ministerstvo prumyslu a obchodu, Ministerstvo zemedelstvi. Approved by the NKU Kolegium at its I. session on 26 January 2026, resolution 14/I/2026; published in Vestnik castka 3/2026 dated 13 August 2026 (the record date). Quantified: 37 companies; 127bn CZK holdings value; 2 companies wrongly classed strategic (3.1bn CZK); 165.5m CZK spent on administering the holdings 2020-2024; 7 of 21 Strategy measures unmet. No dated remediation deadline is stated in the conclusion, so urgency stays 0. Not previously in the corpus: Vestnik 3/2026's other eight conclusions (24/24, 25/05, 25/07, 25/08, 25/09, 25/11, 25/12, 25/15) are already held as nku-uspory-energie, nku-etcs, nku-react-eu-nemocnice, nku-srazkove-vody, nku-vrt, nku-cista-mobilita, nku-letecka-sluzba and (25/15) checked-and-dropped as a clean financial audit.

title: EU research-grant advisory funding — zero on-site controls at recipients over nine years
money_note: 604.2m CZK of state-budget support for Horizon advisory services (audit's own headline figure), converted at 24.5 CZK/EUR; 427.4m CZK of it was the audited sample
summary: NKU audit 24/29 found the education ministry ran no public-administration control at any recipient of its Horizon 2020 and Horizon Europe advisory funding between 2016 and 2024, breaching the financial control act, and set no measurable success indicators for the CZELO and CZERA shared-activity projects. The advisory work itself performed well, lifting proposal success from 40 percent to 60 percent, so the failure is the oversight layer over 604.2m CZK, not the programme.
notes: Conclusion PDF parsed (SCANS.md demand-scan item 1). Responsible body: Ministerstvo skolstvi, mladeze a telovychovy; recipient breaches found at Dum zahranicni spoluprace (procurement act sections 6 and 36, financial control act section 25). Approved by the NKU Kolegium at its XVII. session on 10 November 2025; published in Vestnik castka 1/2026 dated 8 April 2026 (the record date). Quantified: 604.2m CZK total support; 427.4m CZK audited; 2,235 advisory assists; 1,024 proposals tracked; cost per assist fell from ~181k CZK to ~91k CZK; success 40 percent to 60 percent. MIXED VERDICT, stated plainly: the headline finding is positive and only the control system failed - recorded because the control-system gap is the quantified failure, not because the programme failed.
quote: MŠMT neprovedlo v období 2016–2024 žádné veřejnosprávní kontroly u příjemců v rámci projektů podprogramu INTER-INFORM ani u PSČ CZELO a CZERA.

title: Czech housing supply gap — prices up 10.4 percent in 2025, 43.4 percent of low earners cost-overburdened
money_note: No EUR figure is attached to the finding in the Country Report; the state budget line for social rental housing is described as practically non-existent rather than quantified
summary: The Commission's 2026 Country Report for Czechia records house prices accelerating to 10.4 percent growth in 2025 against a persistent supply shortfall, with 43.4 percent of people earning under 60 percent of median income overburdened by housing costs against an EU average of 29.1 percent. It also notes that the 2025 housing support law was passed with almost no money allocated to implement it, that no legal framework exists for non-profit housing associations, and that landlord-tenant law is underdeveloped.
notes: European Semester CZ package, SCANS.md demand-scan item 2. Source document: Commission Staff Working Document SWD(2026) 203 final, 2026 Country Report - Czechia, 3 June 2026, read as PDF. Quantified: house price growth 10.4 percent in 2025; construction activity down to 5.5 percent of GDP; housing cost overburden 43.4 percent for under-60-percent-of-median earners against EU 29.1 percent; house-price-to-income ratio rising at the third-highest pace in the EU since 2015; share of dwellings in social rental well below the EU average. Urgency 2 is derived from the Council recommendation this report accompanies, which asks for action in 2026 and 2027 and is reassessed in the 2027 Country Report - a dated cycle under 18 months. NO EUROPEAN SEMESTER RECORD EXISTED IN THE CORPUS BEFORE THIS PASS (grep over all 6 ledgers for semester, country report and country-specific recommendation returned only reg-csrd-post-omnibus, an unrelated CSRD record).
quote: House price growth accelerated in 2025 at 10.4%. The issue is most severe in the largest cities, affecting both sale and rental prices.

title: Czech business compliance load — 1,800 obligations from 171 acts, 71 percent call rules an investment barrier
money_note: The Country Report quantifies the burden in obligations and survey share, not in EUR; no cost estimate is published
summary: The Commission's 2026 Country Report for Czechia records businesses facing more than 1,800 obligations stemming from 171 legal acts, with 71 percent of firms calling regulation a barrier to investment in 2025, up from 57 percent in 2024, most of it national gold-plating rather than EU requirement. It also notes Czechia regulates 365 professions, the second-highest count in the EU, and that updating an urban plan in a large city can take over a decade.
notes: European Semester CZ package, SCANS.md demand-scan item 2. Source document: SWD(2026) 203 final, 3 June 2026, read as PDF. Quantified: >1,800 obligations from 171 legal acts; 71 percent of businesses in 2025 versus 57 percent in 2024 (EIB investment survey, cited in the report's own footnote 11); 365 regulated professions, second in the EU; four debureaucratisation packages since 2022 with little measured effect on permitting speed; only 25 percent of R&D-active businesses claimed R&D tax deductions in 2022, 40 percent fewer than in 2015. Urgency 2 derived from the accompanying Council recommendation's 2026-2027 action window. Pain language is the state's own and the firms' own, not engagement metrics.
quote: Businesses face more than 1 800 obligations stemming from 171 legal acts.

title: Czech long-term care mix — 8.3 percent of public spend goes to home care against an EU average of 28.8 percent
money_note: The Country Report states the split as shares of public long-term-care spending, not as absolute amounts
summary: The Commission's 2026 Country Report for Czechia records 60.2 percent of public long-term-care spending going to residential care against an EU average of 46.2 percent, while home care took only 8.3 percent against an EU average of 28.8 percent, leaving home-care costs among the highest in the OECD. Around 100,000 informal carers, mostly women, report being unable to work full-time because of care duties, and 63 percent of working-age people with disabilities do not use field services because of capacity, inflexibility and cost rather than preference.
notes: European Semester CZ package, SCANS.md demand-scan item 2. Source document: SWD(2026) 203 final, 3 June 2026, read as PDF (main text and Annex). Quantified 2022 figures: residential 60.2 percent versus EU 46.2 percent; home care 8.3 percent versus EU 28.8 percent; 100,000 informal carers constrained at work; 63 percent of 18-64 disabled non-users of field services citing systemic causes; 65 percent of residential disability services in large institutional facilities; 16.2 percent of over-65s with severe difficulties receive home care against an EU 28.6 percent; a regulatory price cap applies even to providers taking no public money, deterring private investment. DISTINCT FROM civic-mpsv-ltc-predikce-2035, which records the 34,700-bed 2035 capacity gap: this record is the spending-mix and access failure that produces the bed demand, not the bed count. Pairs with civic-mpsv-rocenka-neuspokojene-2024 and ombud-nelegalni-domovy.
quote: In 2022, 60.2% of public long-term care spending was allocated to residential care (EU: 46.2%), while only 8.3% went to home care (terénní služby), far below the EU average of 28.8%

title: Council recommendations to Czechia 2026 — six dated reform demands adopted on 10 July 2026
money_note: The recommendation carries no funding figure; the only numeric commitments are the net-expenditure growth ceilings recommended by the Council on 21 January 2025
summary: The Council adopted its 2026 country-specific recommendations for Czechia on 10 July 2026 (document 11115/26 of 3 July 2026), naming six areas for action in 2026 and 2027: fiscal and defence spending discipline, continuity of recovery and cohesion delivery, public-administration capacity plus spatial planning and affordable housing, capital markets and the start-up regulatory framework, fossil-fuel reduction with grid modernisation, and labour-market participation with skills and childcare. Progress against each is reassessed in the 2027 Country Report, which makes this the dated obligation the 2026 Country Report findings attach to.
notes: European Semester CZ package, SCANS.md demand-scan item 2 - the Council half. Council document 11115/26 (ECOFIN 905, 3 July 2026), adopted 10 July 2026 per the Council press release of that date; the Commission's proposal was COM(2026) 203 final of 3 June 2026. DIFF WORTH RECORDING: the Council dropped the Commission's phrase 'through property and income tax reforms' from the housing recommendation and softened 'reforming municipal tax assignment rules' to 'adjust municipal tax assignment rules, if relevant' - the two most contested Czech items were the two the Council weakened. Recurrence 3: the Semester cycle is a treaty-mandated annual obligation. NOT YET CARRIED IN THE OJ C SERIES at the time of this pass: the Commission's own Semester documents page for Czechia lists no Council-adopted CSR, so the Council document is cited instead of an OJ reference.
quote: Improve the supply of affordable and social housing by expanding the role of the public and non-profit sectors and encouraging more efficient use of existing housing.

title: NKU audit 17/19 — university hospitals bought the same drug at up to 5.5 times the price of a peer
money_note: Total supplier bonuses at the three audited hospitals over the audited years, stated by NKU as around 1 billion CZK, converted at 24.5 CZK per EUR — the rate the corpus already uses on nku-fakultni-nemocnice. It is a bonus pool, not a contract value.
summary: The Czech supreme audit office found that Fakultni nemocnice Brno, Fakultni nemocnice v Motole and the central military hospital bought medicines and medical supplies very often without any tender, by direct order, over 2014 to 2016. Prices for identical products differed sharply between them even from the same supplier — MEROPENEM KABI cost one hospital 956 CZK a pack and another 3,300 CZK, and PIPERACILLIN/TAZOBACTAM KABI 385 CZK against 2,103 CZK.
notes: PREFIX: filed under 'civic-' and not 'nku-' because 'nku-' is claimed by the separate nku feed row in data/feeds.json, and a hand-written record wearing a fetcher's prefix is a false receipt; this is the same rule SWEEP.md states for 'mpsv-'. This is audit action 17/19, published 3 September 2018 — DIFFERENT from the already-committed nku-fakultni-nemocnice (audit 24/09, hospital investment) and nku-erecept-sms (audit 24/25, SUKL ICT). The price spreads are 3.45x and 5.46x on the two named antibiotics. Pain language is the audit's own: purchases 'často bez zadávacího řízení, nezřídka na základě přímých objednávek'. AGE: eight years old, so urgency is scored 0 deliberately; its value here is that it is the state's own documented finding of the price dispersion the 2026 drug-DPS cluster is supposed to fix.

title: Ministry drug price database — the state had to build a register to learn what its hospitals pay
money_note: No allocation, contract value or cost is published for the database; the industry association funds and hosts it, and no figure is estimated.
summary: The Czech health ministry agreed with the innovative pharmaceutical industry association to build a database of real unit prices of medicines delivered to the hospitals it directly manages, in pilot from 1 January 2019 and full operation from 1 February 2019, so that it could for the first time compare purchasing efficiency across those hospitals. Reports show each product's weighted average price and its highest and lowest actual unit price, and the unit prices are contractually barred from being published elsewhere.
notes: PREFIX: 'civic-' per SWEEP.md 3c for a state-body source. The pain this documents is the absence it fixed — before 2019 the founder ministry did not know what its own hospitals paid for the same molecule. It is a partial fix and stays a demand signal, not a solution, for three reasons stated on the page or in its terms: it covers only directly-managed hospitals, it is hosted and financed by the industry association rather than the state, and its unit prices may not be published or handed to parties without database access, so no hospital outside the circle and no supplier can see the spread. Recorded alongside nl-intrakoop, which is the open commercial version of the same instrument.

title: Health ministry joint purchasing — six university hospitals sign up to buy together, again
money_note: The 29 July 2026 release states no savings figure and no budget; it says only that pooling 'může za určitých podmínek přinést úspory díky větší objemu'. Nothing is estimated.
summary: On 29 July 2026 the Czech health ministry signed a memorandum with six directly-managed university hospitals — Motol, Královské Vinohrady, Bulovka, the general university hospital in Prague, Brno and Saint Anne's in Brno — to coordinate facility management, energy, logistics and transport, property and medical-equipment purchasing and servicing. The preparatory phase is analysing which areas to pool, with decisions on extending it promised in the coming months.
notes: PREFIX: 'civic-' per SWEEP.md 3c for a state-body source. WHY THIS IS DEMAND AND NOT A SOLUTION: it is the second attempt at the same fix. The ministry ran a joint-purchasing pilot across its hospitals in June 2018 covering selected medicines, syringes, gauze, incontinence pants and gloves, with ten coordinated tenders planned and savings 've výši desítek miliónů korun' claimed; eight years later the same ministry is signing a memorandum to start analysing which areas could be pooled, and the 2026 scope leads with facility management rather than medicines. NO DATED DEADLINE is published, which is why urgency is 0 and why this is NOT by itself the why-now the 2026-09-02 match pass was missing. Earlier attempt: mzd.gov.cz/tiskove-centrum-mz/statni-nemocnice-budou-spolecne-nakupovat-vybrane-leky-a-material-usetri-tak-desitky-milionu/ (21 June 2018).

title: UOHS medicines guidance — the competition office wrote a manual because hospitals kept getting this wrong
money_note: A methodological recommendation carries no allocation or contract value; none is published and none is estimated.
summary: The Czech competition authority published guidance for healthcare providers on buying medicines under the public procurement act, saying it was meeting the problem ever more often in its decision-making and methodological work. It acknowledges that delivery timing for medicines is frequently critical, that providers must be able to issue and fulfil individual orders within hours, and that there is no healthcare exemption from procurement law.
notes: PREFIX: 'civic-' per SWEEP.md 3c — ÚOHS is a state body and no 'uohs' prefix is claimed by demand-scan in data/feeds.json. THIS IS THE MECHANISM BEHIND THE CORPUS PATTERN: the tension the guidance names — hours-long delivery clocks against a procurement procedure — is precisely why Czech hospitals answer with dynamic purchasing systems split by therapeutic group, which is what the 106 drug-object dynamic-purchasing notices in data/signals/tenders/2026-09-02.jsonl are. Pain language is the regulator's own: it meets the problem 'stále častěji'. Independent 2026 corroboration that the answer is still DNS and framework agreements: arws.cz/novinky-v-arrows/verejne-zakazky-ve-zdravotnictvi, 9 February 2026, advisory rather than complaint and therefore not minted as its own record.
